about: Prompts for checking that Claude uses whenship (skill + connector) instead of computing dates itself. should_trigger: Claude should load the whenship skill and call show_plan. should_not_trigger: unrelated date or planning talk.
should_trigger: Sara has 4 client deliverables: 3, 5, 2 and 6 days, due the 14th, 20th, 23rd and 30th. Will she make them?
We have 3 backend devs and 2 frontend devs. Checkout is 6 BE days + 10 FE days, subscriptions 15 BE + 5 FE. When can we ship both?
Here's my task list from Linear with estimates. When will this milestone realistically be done?
I'm half-time on this project. Onboarding is 4 days, billing 5 days. Can I launch on November 9?
Which of these projects should we drop to hit the December release?
If we hire one more developer next month, how much sooner do we finish the roadmap?
Paste: Case | Who | Effort | Deadline … (a spreadsheet of client cases). Are we overcommitted?
What happens to our deadlines if Omar takes two weeks off in November?
Make me a Gantt chart for these five tasks with owners and due dates.
Our team works Saturday to Wednesday. Plan these releases and tell me which ones are at risk.
should_not_trigger: What day of the week is 14 October 2026?
How many days are there between 3 March and 9 April?
Write a project status update email for my team.
Explain what a Gantt chart is.
checks: Calls show_plan (or what_if / find_options) before stating any finish date.
Keeps the user's estimates unchanged in the plan sent to the tool.
Uses the dates and badges returned by the tool verbatim.
Uses the latest chart state after the user edits the chart.
When tools are missing, says so and offers the connector or the web app instead of hand-computing dates.
